description: Every scripted fetch of bank.gov.ua and data.gov.ua HTML pages attempted in this run returned HTTP 403 Forbidden (tried: /ua/supervision/registers, data.gov.ua/organization/natsionalnyi-bank-ukrayiny).

result.result_summary: No page body retrieved from either domain via plain fetch. Both domains are heavily and currently linked from search results and third-party sites, and NBU PDF assets under /admin_uploads/ were indexed normally, so the 403 is almost certainly WAF/bot filtering rather than a dead or moved resource. These sources are recorded as UNVERIFIED-BUT-PRESUMED-LIVE, not dead.

why_it_matters: The two most important domains in this cell cannot be collected with a naive HTTP client. The collection pipeline must budget for a headless browser (or realistic headers/session) for HTML, and should prefer the CKAN API for data.gov.ua and direct /admin_uploads/ file paths for bank.gov.ua.

description: Two hostnames surfaced in search results failed DNS resolution during this run: www.prostir.gov.ua and new.bank.gov.ua.

result.result_summary: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for both. The apex prostir.gov.ua resolved and served content normally, so the www. host is simply not configured. new.bank.gov.ua appeared in an English search result (a redesign/staging host for the NBU site) but did not resolve from this environment — it may be geo-restricted, retired, or not yet public.

why_it_matters: Collection configs must pin prostir.gov.ua WITHOUT the www prefix. And an NBU site redesign under a 'new.' host would relocate every register URL in this cell — worth re-testing, because a silent migration would break the whole pointer layer.

description: No actual register CONTENT (a list of named ТОПП / payment institutions / e-money issuers) was retrieved in this run — only the register landing pages, dataset pages and their documented locations.

result.result_summary: Search engines surfaced the register pages and the open-data dataset identifiers, but the underlying tables and files were not opened. The only concrete counts obtained were from PROSTIR's own About page (48 participants; ~516k cards; ~15k ATMs; ~603k POS terminals; ~23k self-service terminals) and a search-derived claim of 47 banks + 2 non-bank participants, which are inconsistent with each other and must be re-derived from the register itself.

why_it_matters: This is a source-scouting cell, so pointers are the deliverable — but downstream cells must not treat any actor count in this slice as established. The participant-count discrepancy is a concrete example of why the register file, not a summary page, has to be the citation of record.

description: English-language searching for the NBU registers returned mostly Wikipedia, law-firm commentary (Wolf Theiss, Kinstellar, BMG) and news rather than the registers themselves.

result.result_summary: The English NBU pages exist (/en/supervision/payment-services/fps, /en/payments, /en/supervision/licensing-nonbanking/lic-financial-services) but the register attachments and the RPI contents are predominantly Ukrainian-only. Several search results explicitly noted that English sections have reduced content.

why_it_matters: Confirms that Ukrainian-language collection is not optional for this cell — an English-only pipeline would miss the actual name-lists entirely and would systematically under-count non-bank and technological operators. It also means transliteration of institution names must be handled deliberately.

description: The custodianship of the Ukrainian financial registers has changed repeatedly and the legal framework was replaced mid-stream.

result.result_summary: Confirmed from multiple sources: Держфінпослуг created the ДРФУ in 2003; functions moved to Нацкомфінпослуг in 2013; the 2020 'split' transferred them to the NBU; the NSSMC ceased maintaining its share of the ДРФУ around 15.01.2024; and the Law 'Про платіжні послуги' replaced the old payment-systems register with the Реєстр платіжної інфраструктури, with entries migrated automatically and the new registration order effective 01.08.2024.

why_it_matters: Historical extracts and any pre-2024 vendor/competitor list are keyed to registers that no longer exist under the same name or custodian. Time-series work must map old register identities onto new ones or it will read migrations as market entries and exits.

description: No Ukrainian-language register or official term was located for a public list of ATM/self-service or branch-automation SUPPLIERS specifically.

result.result_summary: Searches around the register vocabulary produced no equivalent of a supplier/vendor accreditation register for banking hardware. Ukraine appears to have no licensing regime for such vendors, so they exist in no sector register — only in the ЄДР by KVED, in Дія.Сіті if they qualify, and in Prozorro award records.

why_it_matters: The cell's premise — that registers give a complete actor census — holds for regulated actors (banks, PSPs, ТОПП) but NOT for unregulated technology suppliers. Enumerating Printec's direct competitor set requires the Prozorro + ЄДР/KVED + Дія.Сіті triangulation described in the candidates, and this gap should be stated explicitly rather than left implicit.

description: No dedicated Sense Bank procurement/tender page was surfaced by Ukrainian-language search. Sense Bank was nationalised in 2023 and searches returned only privatisation news (Ministry of Finance preparing sale of state stakes in Sense Bank and Ukrgasbank), not a supplier/tender section.

result.result_summary: Sense Bank tender disclosures could not be located as a distinct source; its Prozorro buyer entity was also not confirmed by EDRPOU in this run.

why_it_matters: Sense Bank is one of the four state-owned banks named in the cell scope; without its buyer identifier its ATM/POS/software procurement is invisible to any pipeline keyed on buyer codes.

description: Direct Ukrainian-language keyword searching for ATM supply tenders ('банкомат', 'постачання банкоматів') via a general web search engine returned only generic Prozorro portal pages, no individual award records.

result.result_summary: General web search is a poor discovery channel for individual Prozorro item-level records; the portal's own content is largely not surfaced by external indexes.

why_it_matters: Confirms that item-level ATM/POS discovery must be done through the API or the BI module with CPV filters, not through search-engine keyword hunting. This is a method constraint, not an absence of data.

description: The specific CPV codes covering ATMs, self-service kiosks and POS terminals were not confirmed in this run; only CPV 72261000-2 (software support services) was observed on a real record.

result.result_summary: One confirmed CPV; the hardware-side CPV set remains unmapped.

why_it_matters: CPV is the primary machine filter for the whole cell. Without a verified hardware CPV list, an API harvest will either over-collect or silently miss the ATM/POS categories.

description: Several POS-related Prozorro records found are public bodies buying acquiring SERVICES from banks (bank supplies mobile POS terminals as part of a settlement service), not banks buying POS hardware from vendors.

result.result_summary: The phrase 'POS-термінал' in Prozorro frequently denotes acquiring services, not terminal supply.

why_it_matters: A naive keyword harvest on 'POS-термінал' will be dominated by acquiring-service tenders and will badly distort any vendor market map unless the buyer/seller direction is classified.

description: PrivatBank's procurement is reported by search results to have moved to zakupivli24.pb.ua; neither that site nor tender.privatbank.ua was fetched, so structure, coverage and whether award results are published remain unknown.

result.result_summary: PrivatBank procurement portals recorded as unverified hypotheses, not confirmed sources.

why_it_matters: PrivatBank owns the largest ATM/POS estate in Ukraine; a gap here is the largest single blind spot in the cell.

description: Search-engine queries in both uk and en for Ukrainian bank vacancies explicitly naming 'SmartVista' (BPC) returned no live vacancy pages, only generic djinni/board landing pages.

result.result_summary: SmartVista appears as a platform name in vendor/reference material but was not surfaced in any indexed Ukrainian vacancy text during this scouting pass.

why_it_matters: Absence in search indexes is not absence in the market — vacancy bodies on work.ua/robota.ua/djinni are often poorly indexed. On-site keyword search on each board is required before concluding BPC has no UA footprint.

description: No dedicated engineering/tech blog was found for monobank/Fintech Band or PrivatBank via uk-language search; results returned press coverage (ITC.ua, NV, Forbes.ua) and Wikipedia rather than a first-party engineering blog.

result.result_summary: Bank-owned engineering blogs appear to be largely absent in Ukraine; technical disclosure happens instead through DOU articles, podcasts and conference talks.

why_it_matters: The 'bank engineering blog' branch of this cell is thin; collection effort should be reallocated to DOU editorial/podcast content and vacancy texts, and to conference-talk listings, rather than to first-party blogs.

description: No vacancy or careers page was located for Ukrainian PSPs Fondy, Portmone, EasyPay or Concord-related acquirers in this pass; the PSP query returned only UPC.

result.result_summary: PSP-side hiring signal remains uncovered; only the bank and third-party-processor sides were mapped.

why_it_matters: PSP/acquirer stack signals (gateway, tokenisation, POS estate) are a distinct and commercially important layer that this pass did not reach.

description: No page was fetched or liveness-tested in this pass; all URLs come from search-result listings only.

result.result_summary: All candidate URLs are provided at stated confidence without any liveness claim.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve every URL, especially bot-defended domains (LinkedIn, Indeed, djinni) where a 403 should be read as bot-defended-but-live rather than dead.

description: No Ukrainian aggregator was found that indexes contracts of PRIVATE (non-state-owned) banks. Prozorro, spending.gov.ua and the aggregators built on them cover public buyers and state/communal enterprises only; private bank–vendor contracts surface only indirectly (litigation, commercial tender boards, vendor press releases).

result.result_summary: Searches in uk and en for private/commercial bank procurement disclosure returned only commercial tender marketplaces (SmartTender, E-Tender, Zakupivli24), not a contract register.

why_it_matters: Supplier mapping for private banks — the majority of the Ukrainian banking market by count — cannot be done from aggregators alone and needs litigation and commercial-tender triangulation.

description: The three main aggregators (Clarity Project, YouControl, VKURSI) all gate their most valuable views — full dossiers, KVED catalogues, connection graphs, exports — behind paid subscriptions, and their ToS restrict bulk automated collection.

result.result_summary: Free tiers confirmed to exist but with limited fields; licensed API products (YouScore, Opendatabot API, VKURSI API, Clarity App licence) identified as the sanctioned route.

why_it_matters: Budget and licensing decisions are a prerequisite for systematic collection in this cell; scraping is a legal and continuity risk.

description: No page in this cell was fetched directly; all findings come from search-result metadata and snippets. URLs are provided with confidence scores but liveness is unverified.

result.result_summary: Registry portals such as usr.minjust.gov.ua are known to be session- and e-signature-gated and are likely to appear unreachable to automated fetchers without being dead.

why_it_matters: Downstream liveness checks should not mark e-signature-gated or bot-defended registry portals as dead on a single failed fetch.

description: No World Bank/IFC project in Ukraine dedicated specifically to 'payment systems modernisation' surfaced in search. The closest confirmed World Bank Ukraine appraisal precedent in the IT/financial-administration space is the State Tax Service Modernization Project (Report 25875-UA, 2003), and IFC's Ukraine payments-adjacent work appears as advisory projects (credit reporting, digital financial services) rather than a named payments programme.

result.result_summary: Searched both seed phrasing and document-portal phrasing; found financial-sector rehabilitation DPLs, tax administration IT, and IFC risk-sharing/advisory disclosures, but no standalone payment-infrastructure operation.

why_it_matters: Collection for this cell must not wait for a project named 'payment systems'; the relevant scope sits inside broader financial-sector, PFM and digital-government operations, so keyword rules need to be widened accordingly.

description: USAID's Ukraine financial-sector programme pages (as relayed by the NBU) describe workstreams but do not name implementing contractors or subcontractors, and no USAID-side award page for a payments-specific Ukraine programme was located.

result.result_summary: Programme descriptions found for USAID Financial Sector Reform, Financial Sector Transformation and Investment for Business Resilience (IBR); none carried vendor/contract data.

why_it_matters: Vendor identification for the US-funded slice must be done by joining programme names to federal award databases (USAspending) and oversight reports rather than from programme communications.

description: DevelopmentAid mirrors donor tenders and awards relevant to Ukraine but gates contractor and value detail behind a subscription.

result.result_summary: Public listing pages show title, donor, country and sector only.

why_it_matters: It can be used for discovery but cannot serve as the citable evidence layer; every lead must be resolved back to the originating donor portal.

description: No established Ukrainian-language term or portal was found for EBRD client-side procurement notices; Ukrainian coverage of EBRD tenders is journalistic or beneficiary-institution relay rather than a systematic Ukrainian-language notice feed. ECEPP itself appears to operate in English only.

result.result_summary: Ukrainian queries returned ministry portfolio pages, news tags and one-off institutional announcements, not a Ukrainian notice register for IFI procurement.

why_it_matters: Ukrainian-language monitoring for this cell must be alerting-based (keyword watch across gov.ua and media) rather than register-based, except for the МТД register and Prozorro donor module which are genuinely Ukrainian-language systematic sources.

description: No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live by me; all were taken from search-result metadata and snippets. Several (ECEPP notice permalinks, EU Funding & Tenders portal, TED) are JavaScript-heavy or session-bound and may present differently or 403 to naive crawlers.

result.result_summary: Liveness unverified by design; deterministic verification pass required.

why_it_matters: Any 403/timeout on these should be read as bot defence, not as a dead source.

description: No consolidated, publicly published NBU list of open-banking PILOT participants was located — only the general Payment Infrastructure Register plus press reporting that PrivatBank and PUMB were authorised for PIS/AIS in Q1 2026 with two further applications pending.

result.result_summary: Searched uk terms 'пілот', 'учасники пілоту', 'пілотний проєкт відкритий банкінг' alongside NBU/open-banking terms; regulator pages describe the regime and register, not a named pilot cohort.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumes a published participant/pilot list; in Ukraine the equivalent artefact is the authorisation register, so collection must be keyed to register diffs rather than to a pilot page that may not exist.

description: No public source found that names the technology vendor behind the NBU's own SEP-4.1 instant-payment core, nor a tender for it.

result.result_summary: uk searches combining СЕП / миттєві платежі with постачальник, вендор, тендер, закупівля returned only NBU descriptive pages, Wikipedia and news about the go-live; NBU as a central bank does not publish this via Prozorro in an obvious way.

why_it_matters: The central-bank rail is the single largest technology decision in this cell and it appears opaque; supplier intelligence for SEP will have to come from conference talks, vendor references or staff/LinkedIn signals rather than documents.

description: Searched for Corezoid/Middleware (the PrivatBank-descended platform vendor) and Mastercard as open-banking suppliers in Ukraine; no evidence surfaced in this pass.

result.result_summary: The uk query naming Corezoid and Mastercard returned generic open-banking explainers and PrivatBank's own developer portal; the search engine explicitly noted no results for those vendors in a Ukrainian open-banking tender context.

why_it_matters: Prevents a plausible-sounding but unevidenced vendor claim from entering the actor map; retest later with Ukrainian brand spellings (Корезоїд, Мідлвер) and via bank job ads.

description: UPC's corporate site (upc.ua) was inferred from third-party coverage rather than fetched in this pass; the exact URL and its news-section path are unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: UPC's role as NBU-registered technology operator and Tietoevry partner is well evidenced from Tietoevry, Cision, Finextra, IBS Intelligence and Wolf Theiss, but the primary domain was not opened here.

why_it_matters: The liveness pass should treat upc.ua as a hypothesis to confirm, not as a verified endpoint.

description: For consent-management and API-gateway product categories there is no settled Ukrainian term; the market uses English-in-Ukrainian ('консент', 'API-шлюз', 'відкритий банкінг API') inconsistently.

result.result_summary: Ukrainian sources default to English product nouns transliterated or untranslated, so local-language queries for these subcategories are unreliable and under-recall.

why_it_matters: Collection queries for these vendor categories must run bilingual token mixes rather than pure Ukrainian, or they will miss suppliers.

description: Searched specifically for Reuters reporting on a Ukrainian bank IT/technology supplier contract (Oschadbank, PrivatBank, Ukreximbank).

result.result_summary: No Reuters item on a technology supplier contract was found. Results returned governance/privatisation material instead (supervisory-board recruitment competitions, state-bank privatisation debate) from Komersant, VoxUkraine, Atlantic Council and Kyiv Post.

why_it_matters: Confirms the general wires do not cover banking-IT procurement in Ukraine at deal level; vendor-technology intelligence must come from specialist trade press (Finextra, The Paypers, FinTech Futures) and from procurement/tender sources in other cells, not from Reuters/Bloomberg.

description: Searched for a vendor-neutral, paid or free analyst market report specifically titled/scoped to the Ukrainian banking-technology or POS/self-service vendor landscape (Gartner/Forrester/IDC/GlobalData style).

result.result_summary: No Ukraine-specific vendor-landscape report was located in this pass. The closest vendor-neutral artefacts found are the UAFIC Ukrainian Fintech Catalog, the OECD financial-markets mapping and IBSi's generic payments-vendor directories — none of which segments POS/branch-automation suppliers by share.

why_it_matters: The cell brief anticipates 'vendor-neutral analyst notes'; their apparent absence for Ukraine means competitive share must be reconstructed bottom-up from deal announcements, tenders and company sites rather than bought off the shelf.

description: Assessed FinTech Futures for Ukraine-specific core-banking or channel-technology contract reporting.

result.result_summary: Section indexes and the outlet's Ukraine relevance were confirmed, but no Ukraine-specific core-banking contract article surfaced in this pass; results skewed to generic Ukrainian IT-outsourcing listicles from low-authority sites (scroll.media, thistradinglife.com) rather than the outlet itself.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations: FinTech Futures should be monitored by vendor name rather than by country, because Ukrainian wins are more likely to appear inside a global vendor's announcement than under a Ukraine tag.

description: Reuters and Bloomberg were not fetched; their liveness and gating are asserted from general knowledge only.

result.result_summary: Both recorded as blocked=true with blocker_type paywall/bot-defence, but this is a hypothesis for the verification pass, not an observed 403 or 404.

why_it_matters: Avoids recording well-known wires as dead or open on no evidence; the deterministic liveness pass should resolve their actual status and the value of a licensed feed.

description: The acronym 'IBS' resolves to at least three distinct entities relevant to this run.

result.result_summary: IBS Intelligence (UK fintech analyst house), I.B.S. / Innovative Banking Systems (Kyiv cash-automation integrator, ibs.kiev.ua), and FIS's 'IBS — Integrated Banking Solution' product all appear in the same result set.

why_it_matters: Automated collection keyed on 'IBS Ukraine' will conflate an analyst source with a direct competitor. Queries must be disambiguated by domain, and the glossary must record all three.

description: No evidence found of an EMV Level 1/Level 2 accredited test laboratory physically located in Ukraine. Searches in Ukrainian for 'сертифікація платіжних терміналів EMV Україна лабораторія' returned only general accreditation registers (NAAU), metrology bodies (Укрметртестстандарт, UCRF) and terminal resellers.

result.result_summary: EMVCo-recognised labs appear to be foreign; Ukrainian terminal certification looks like scheme/processor-level onboarding (ПРОСТІР via УкрКарт, Visa/Mastercard via processors) rather than domestic EMVCo lab accreditation.

why_it_matters: Means terminal certification evidence must be sourced from EMVCo's own approval lists and from processor/scheme onboarding announcements, not from a Ukrainian lab registry.

description: No Ukraine-filtered public extract of the PCI SSC QSA/ASV directory was retrievable through search; the directory is a JavaScript search UI and country-filtered result pages are not indexed.

result.result_summary: Ukrainian QSA presence had to be inferred from firms' own claims (Compliance Control, Allcontrols, IT Specialist, System Management) rather than from the authoritative registry.

why_it_matters: Self-claimed QSA status is unreliable; the registry must be queried via browser automation before any firm is treated as an accredited assessor.

description: The Держспецзв'язку 'Перелік атестованих аудиторів інформаційної безпеки' is referenced in official news items but a stable direct URL to the register itself was not located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Register existence confirmed via cip.gov.ua news; canonical page/PDF location unverified.

why_it_matters: This register is the highest-value named-entity list in the cell; locating its canonical URL should be a priority follow-up.

description: No public bank IT-audit report naming specific systems and suppliers was found. Ukrainian bank annual reports and NBU supervisory disclosures surfaced in search do not publish IT-audit findings at supplier granularity.

result.result_summary: Supplier names must be reconstructed indirectly from PCI compliance pages, procurement records and CERT advisories.

why_it_matters: Removes an assumed evidence path; raises the weight of Prozorro and CERT-UA as substitutes.

description: Direct fetch of https://www.universalbank.com.ua/ (monobank's licence-holding bank) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.

result.result_summary: 403 on a site that is clearly live and indexed. Hypothesis: WAF/bot defence, not a dead site. Recorded as unverified/bot-defended, not dead.

why_it_matters: Universal Bank is the only formal corporate channel for the monobank ecosystem; if collection uses plain HTTP fetching it will silently miss this actor entirely.

description: No dedicated press-centre / прес-центр path was located for А-Банк (a-bank.com.ua) or, in its final period, for Банк Конкорд (concord.ua) — only general /about pages plus third-party aggregator feeds.

result.result_summary: A-Bank news reaches the public mainly via finance.ua, minfin.com.ua, nv.ua and mind.ua rather than a first-party newsroom.

why_it_matters: For these two actors the buyer-announcement route this cell relies on is weak; vendor relationships must be inferred from aggregators, awards entries and vendor-side claims instead, which lowers attribution confidence.

description: Банк Конкорд was liquidated — DGF stopped payments 11.03.2026 and completed liquidation 05.05.2026 per NBU/DGF reporting relayed by NV and Minfin.

result.result_summary: Concord is an archival actor only; its press channel cannot be a forward-looking source.

why_it_matters: The cell definition lists Concord as a live target. Collection design must reclassify it as historical (Wayback-only) and instead track where its fintech/BaaS clients migrated — that migration is itself a vendor-relationship signal.

description: Across the uk-language searches, private-bank press items overwhelmingly announce the capability (mobile banking, AI, HR&Payroll, Open Banking) without naming the supplier; only PUMB (MiddleWare/Corezoid) and group-level OTP (Intellect Design Arena, Iliad Solutions) yielded explicit vendor names.

result.result_summary: Buyer-side announcements confirm that a project happened but usually not who delivered it.

why_it_matters: The cell's core premise — that banks name vendors voluntarily — holds only partially. Vendor-side newsrooms and case-study pages must be paired with every bank feed to close the attribution gap.

description: No RSS/Atom feed or public API was confirmed for any of the bank press centres in this cell during this pass.

result.result_summary: Only HTML listing pages were observed (raiffeisen.ua/about/press, about.pumb.ua/presscenter, en.otpbank.com.ua/about/news, credit-agricole.ua/.../novini, procreditbank.com.ua/press-center).

why_it_matters: Collection must be built on HTML crawling with change-detection rather than feed subscription, raising maintenance cost and breakage risk on site redesigns.

description: Local-language (uk) search was used for every actor in the cell except the OTP group-level vendor announcements and the Iliad/Intellect items, which exist only in English.

result.result_summary: 5 of 6 executed searches were uk or uk/en mixed; 1 was en-only (OTP group technology partnerships).

why_it_matters: Confirms local-language coverage was met for the buyer-side channel; the English-only gap is on the vendor side, where UA-language equivalents genuinely do not exist.

description: No dedicated Ukrainian ATM / cash-handling / cash-in-transit industry association with a public member directory was located. Searched in Ukrainian using 'асоціація інкасації', 'готівковий обіг', 'банкомати', 'перевезення цінностей'; results returned only banking associations (АУБ, НАБУ), a commercial cash-automation vendor (avtokassa.com), and Oschadbank's own collection service page — i.e. individual market participants rather than a sector body.

result.result_summary: Ukrainian-language search returned bank associations and vendors, not a cash-handling association; the closest structural analogue found is APITU on the IT-equipment side, and EAST (European, via EMA's partner page) on the ATM-security side.

why_it_matters: The ATM/cash-handling segment is central to hardware vendor and competitor mapping (Printec's own segment). Without an association pointer, that segment must be reached via NBU cash-circulation regulation, bank tender records, and EMA's EAST link instead.

description: fintechua.org (both the uk root and /en) returned an essentially empty text body to the markdown fetcher, so the UAFIC member roster could not be read in this pass. No HTTP error code was returned.

result.result_summary: Member page URL (https://fintechua.org/members) confirmed to exist via the search index and via the site's own /about page, but its contents were not retrieved.

why_it_matters: UAFIC is one of the two anchor directories for this cell; treating it as unavailable would blind the vendor/fintech side. The empty body is a rendering hypothesis, not evidence the site is down.

description: nabu.ua returned HTTP 429 on the first fetch of the member-banks page, so the NABU roster and its associate-member/partner pages were not read directly.

result.result_summary: 429 Too Many Requests; the host is live (other nabu.ua URLs appear in the search index and one member-profile page for the fintech association was indexed).

why_it_matters: NABU covers the overwhelming majority of Ukrainian banking assets; its member and partner lists are a core demand-side roster. A single 429 must not be recorded as a dead source.

description: No established Ukrainian-language term was found for a 'self-service terminal / kiosk vendors' industry body; searches with constructed terms ('асоціація виробників терміналів самообслуговування', 'асоціація POS-терміналів') were not productive within this pass and no such association surfaced.

result.result_summary: The Ukrainian association vocabulary for this cell clusters around банки / фінтех / ІТ, with no terminal-hardware sub-body evident.

why_it_matters: Flags a genuine structural gap in the Ukrainian association landscape rather than a search failure — hardware vendors must be reached through APITU, EMA membership, and procurement records.

description: EMA does not appear to publish an English-language member directory; the English-language footprint is limited to Facebook and LinkedIn company pages and third-party profiles. English-only search for 'EMA Ukraine payment systems association members list' returned no English roster page on ema.com.ua.

result.result_summary: The authoritative EMA roster exists only in Ukrainian at /about/members/, confirming that Ukrainian-language collection is mandatory for this cell.

why_it_matters: Any English-only collection pipeline would silently miss the single richest payments-actor roster in Ukraine.

description: No Diebold Nixdorf case study naming a Ukrainian bank was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Searches returned only CEE analogues (Cooperative Bank of Kielce, CSOB) plus indications that DN divested its Russia and Ukraine assets, which plausibly explains removal or non-publication of UA references.

why_it_matters: The largest self-service vendor may have an unrecorded historic Ukrainian installed base; without archived evidence the buyer/supplier gap for ATM hardware stays open.

description: No NCR Atleos, Hyosung or GRG Banking customer reference naming a Ukrainian bank was found.

result.result_summary: Vendor sites returned only generic portfolio pages; ATM-market searches returned market-forecast churn rather than country deals.

why_it_matters: Hardware supplier identity for the Ukrainian ATM fleet remains undetermined from vendor-side disclosure; procurement registers may be the only route.

description: No Temenos, Finastra or Tietoevry press release or customer story naming a Ukrainian bank surfaced.

result.result_summary: Press indexes returned US, Vietnamese and Nordic wins only; targeted Oschadbank/Ukrgasbank queries returned encyclopaedic bank profiles, not vendor content.

why_it_matters: Suggests international core-banking vendors have little disclosed Ukrainian footprint, consistent with local vendor CS Ltd's claimed dominance — a competitive-structure signal worth confirming.

description: No IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient or Thales press release on Ukrainian card issuance or personalisation was found.

result.result_summary: Queries returned global metal-card rankings and unrelated biometric ID contracts in Egypt and Madagascar.

why_it_matters: Card-manufacturing and personalisation supply for Ukraine is undocumented on the vendor side; leaves a topic-level blind spot for the cards value chain.

description: Ukrainian-language searching found local vendor case studies (CS Ltd) and press-release wires but no uk-language pages published by the global vendors themselves.

result.result_summary: Queries using «кейс впровадження», «вендор», «банкомати», «процесинг» surfaced csltd.com.ua, banker.ua, ain.ua; global vendors appear to maintain no Ukrainian-language case-study content.

why_it_matters: Confirms that for global vendors the UA evidence must be collected in English or via local media/procurement, while the local-language layer is dominated by domestic vendors.

description: BPC/SmartVista content is split across a global entity and RU-domiciled successor sites.

result.result_summary: Searches returned bps-iss.ru, bpsprocessing.ru and tadviser.ru rather than a clearly current global BPC case-study library; the UA-relevant history sits mostly in RU-language sources.

why_it_matters: Risks mis-attributing deployments to the wrong corporate entity and raises sanctions/compliance questions about routine collection from those domains.

description: English-language search 'Ukraine ATM authorised distributor partner NCR Diebold Nixdorf Hyosung GRG banking equipment service company' returned only global ATM market-research press releases and parts traders — zero Ukrainian integrators.

result.result_summary: English queries surface global vendor/market-report noise; the Ukrainian integrator layer is effectively invisible in English. Every productive result in this cell came from Ukrainian-language queries.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: this layer must be collected in Ukrainian. Any English-only collection design for UA integrators will return near-zero recall.

description: The seed-named actors 'БС/Банк Сервіс' and 'S-Group' could not be confirmed as Ukrainian banking-equipment companies in either uk or en searches.

result.result_summary: Searches returned unrelated entities (Belarusian BSB Bank, Metinvest Business Service) and no Ukrainian company matching those names in the ATM/POS domain.

why_it_matters: These seed names may be stale, mis-transliterated, or refer to companies that were renamed, liquidated, or lost their web presence after 2022. They should be resolved via EDRPOU name search in Opendatabot/YouControl rather than by web search.

description: Several integrator/service sites (Ban Com Service, UMICON) display partner/client logo walls as images with no alt text or names, and no dedicated /clients or /partners URL.

result.result_summary: Client and partner identities exist on-page but only as unlabelled logo images; Ban Com Service's stats widget even shows a placeholder '0 Customers'.

why_it_matters: Text-only scraping will silently under-collect this cell. Collection design must include image capture plus logo recognition/OCR, otherwise the most valuable signal (which brands and which banks) is lost.

description: 'Printec' resolves to three unrelated Ukrainian web presences: Printec Ukraine LLC (EDRPOU 35442628, the multinational transactional-tech group), printec.com.ua (business-automation hardware), and printec.ua (trade equipment/fasteners retailer).

result.result_summary: Search results conflate all three under the same brand token.

why_it_matters: Entity resolution by brand name alone will produce false attributions in this cell. EDRPOU codes must be the join key, not company names.

description: No Ukraine-specific partner directory was located on the global vendor sites (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Hyosung TNS, GRG Banking) within this pass.

result.result_summary: Partner claims in Ukraine are one-directional: local firms assert the partnership (SSI↔Hyosung TNS/Verifone, SystemGroup↔NCR/Diebold Nixdorf, PUSK↔40+ brands), but no vendor-side confirmation page was found.

why_it_matters: Partner claims in this cell are currently unconfirmed self-assertions. A dedicated pass against vendor 'find a partner' locators is needed to grade claim reliability.

description: No publicly published Visa Ukraine or Mastercard Ukraine 'certified vendor' / 'certified terminal' / 'certified processor' list scoped to Ukraine was located. Scheme certification of terminal hardware, kernels and processors appears to be handled via customer-only portals (Visa Online, Mastercard Connect) and EMVCo/EMV kernel letters of approval, not local public pages.

result.result_summary: Searches in uk and en returned only the global PCI-oriented registries (Visa Global Registry of Service Providers, Mastercard CSPCDP) and unrelated fiscalisation certifications.

why_it_matters: The cell's core promise — a payments-native certified-vendor roster for UA — cannot be met from scheme sites alone; the NBU technological-operator register plus the global PCI registries must serve as proxies.

description: No dedicated Ukrainian-language UnionPay International country site or UA press room was found; UnionPay's Ukraine coverage exists only on its English/Chinese global media centre and via Ukrainian bank and trade-press reporting.

result.result_summary: Local-language query 'картки UnionPay Україна' returned bank and media pages, not a UPI UA property.

why_it_matters: UnionPay activity in UA must be tracked indirectly through banks (PrivatBank, Ukrgasbank) and NBU registers; expect stale and self-reported acceptance figures.

description: The exact public entry point for Mastercard's Compliant Service Provider list (CSPCDP) was not confirmed; secondary sources describe it as a customer database portal.

result.result_summary: Only third-party descriptions found; no confirmed open listing URL.

why_it_matters: Without it, only Visa's registry gives a scheme-side vendor view, halving coverage of the certified-vendor dimension.

description: The NBU Payment Infrastructure Register landing page was identified but the underlying register file (format, URL, machine-readability) was not resolved in this pass; a fetch is needed to determine whether it is HTML, XLSX or PDF.

result.result_summary: Landing page https://bank.gov.ua/ua/supervision/payment-services/reg-ps identified via search snippet only.

why_it_matters: This is the highest-value candidate in the cell; its collection method depends entirely on the file format.

description: PROSTIR participant counts reported by secondary sources are inconsistent (50 banks + 2 non-bank institutions vs 48 participants), and card-in-circulation figures cited are small and undated.

result.result_summary: Conflicting figures across Wikipedia and portal summaries; no authoritative dated figure retrieved.

why_it_matters: Any market-share or participation claim about the national switch must be sourced from prostir.gov.ua or NBU oversight reports directly, never from aggregators.

description: No Ukrainian PSP in this cell was found to publish a structured, dedicated merchant case-study library in the Western SaaS sense.

result.result_summary: Fondy's partners page (fetched directly) carries a single named testimonial (Cloud9 Fulfilment) and no case-study directory; WayForPay, LiqPay, Portmone, iPay and Platon searches surfaced product, tariff and integration pages but no case-study index. Merchant-level evidence has to be reconstructed from integrator blogs, press interviews and marketplace connector lists.

why_it_matters: Case-study collection for UA payments must be an inference pipeline over indirect sources, not a scrape of vendor case-study pages; budget for entity extraction from trade press and agency sites.

description: Canonical URLs for several actors were not confirmed by direct fetch in this pass.

result.result_summary: liqpay.ua, wayforpay.com, ipay.ua, platon.ua, easypay.ua, plata.mono, concordfintech.solutions and mustpay.tech were identified through search result metadata and third-party articles rather than by successful fetch; only fondy.io/gb/partners/ was fetched directly. The exact NBU payment-infrastructure register URL on bank.gov.ua was not pinned down.

why_it_matters: Downstream liveness verification must resolve these, especially plata.mono (branding vs. domain) and the NBU register deep link, before they are treated as stable collection targets.

description: Concord-linked entity status is ambiguous.

result.result_summary: Concord Bank itself appears in Ukrainian Wikipedia/Minfin as a wound-down bank, while Concord Fintech Solutions and MustPay present as live ecosystem/vendor brands. Which legal entity currently holds processing/acquiring capability was not resolved from open search.

why_it_matters: Treating 'Concord' as one live processor would misstate the competitive set; the register lookup is required to disambiguate before any market conclusion.

description: No established Ukrainian-language term was found for a PSP 'partner directory' as a distinct published artefact.

result.result_summary: Queries using 'партнерська програма', 'партнери', 'каталог інтеграцій' returned CMS/module lists and knowledge-base articles rather than partner directories; the artefact type appears not to exist locally under any consistent name.

why_it_matters: Search strategies ported from Western markets will under-retrieve; local retrieval should target 'інтеграції', 'модулі для CMS' and help-centre subdomains instead.

description: Targeted Ukrainian-language search for Mind.ua investigative reporting on bank IT tenders and suppliers ('банки ІТ-рішення тендер постачальник розслідування') returned only procurement-platform company profiles (e-Tender, SmartTender) and a Ukrposhta equipment tender — no bank-specific vendor investigation surfaced.

result.result_summary: Mind.ua confirmed as a relevant outlet, but no evidence in this pass that it runs a recurring bank-IT-procurement investigative line.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumes local media expose contract disputes and tender outcomes; that assumption is unproven for Mind.ua and may need to be met by Prozorro/NBU primary sources handled by other cells.

description: Interfax-Ukraine's full newswire is a paid subscription product; only free news pages and the press-release channel were observed. No pricing, feed format or licence terms were retrieved.

result.result_summary: Free surface confirmed; commercial feed terms unknown.

why_it_matters: If wire coverage proves to be the fastest surface for partnership announcements, a licensing decision is needed before any systematic collection.

description: No RSS/Atom feed URLs were confirmed for any outlet in this cell (finclub.net, psm7.com, mind.ua, epravda.com.ua, ain.ua, banker.ua). Suggested collection methods therefore default to HTML section crawling.

result.result_summary: Feed discovery not performed in this pass.

why_it_matters: Feeds would cut crawl cost and legal exposure substantially; a cheap follow-up check of /rss, /feed and <link rel=alternate> per domain is warranted.

description: delo.ua, historically a major Ukrainian business outlet, did not appear as a live result; the search surfaced delo.net.ua and an English Wikipedia entry about an unrelated DELO instead. Status is a hypothesis, not a verdict — no fetch was attempted.

result.result_summary: delo.ua current status unresolved.

why_it_matters: If delo.ua is defunct or rebranded, its archive may still hold pre-2022 vendor-deal history worth a one-off harvest.

description: No dedicated Ukrainian trade publication was found that focuses specifically on banking core systems, card processing or ATM/self-service estates (the Printec-adjacent niche); coverage of these topics is scattered across general fintech and business outlets.

result.result_summary: No niche bank-technology trade press identified in Ukraine.

why_it_matters: Vendor-level signal for core banking, processing and self-service will have to be assembled from generalist outlets plus vendor and regulator primary sources.

description: No Ukraine-specific ATM / cash-handling / self-service-banking trade exhibition was found. Searches for a UA banking-equipment expo returned only general retail shows (RAU Expo, TradeMaster) and the international EuroShop.

result.result_summary: UA banking-hardware vendors appear to reach buyers through banking forums and international expos rather than a domestic dedicated show.

why_it_matters: The self-service/ATM vendor census for UA cannot be built from a domestic expo exhibitor list; it must be assembled from EMA/BANKIR forum partner tiers, tender data and international expo directories.

description: Sponsor and partner rosters are generally not exposed on conference index pages; on ema.com.ua the conference index fetch returned only event titles and dates, with partner tiers appearing inside individual event pages and post-event news posts.

result.result_summary: Partner-tier data requires per-event page fetches, not index scraping.

why_it_matters: Collection design must budget for one fetch per event (dozens per organiser per year) rather than a single index parse.

description: For FinAwards, Ukrainian Fintech Awards and PSM Awards, search surfaced winner announcements readily but full nominee longlists were not retrievable from search results; nominee pages appear to be replaced by winner pages after each ceremony.

result.result_summary: Winner lists are durable, nominee longlists are not.

why_it_matters: The nominee longlist is the more complete market census; it must be captured live during the voting window (roughly Jan-Mar each year) or recovered from web archives.

description: The acronym НАБУ collides between Незалежна асоціація банків України (banking association) and Національне антикорупційне бюро України (anti-corruption bureau); АУБ/AUB and ЄМА/EMA are also ambiguous in transliteration (EMA vs. European Medicines Agency in English results).

result.result_summary: Local-term searches on these acronyms are noisy without disambiguating qualifiers.

why_it_matters: Automated query expansion must use full names ('Незалежна асоціація банків України', 'Асоціація ЄМА') rather than acronyms, or precision collapses.

description: Only one page was fetched directly (ema.com.ua conferences index); all other URLs come from search-result listings and are recorded unverified by design.

result.result_summary: URLs are candidates with stated confidence, not verified-live endpoints.

why_it_matters: The downstream deterministic liveness pass must check every URL; treat any 403/timeout as bot-defence, not death.
